A01:
# Task A01: update your display name
Add an accessible display-name form to dashboard settings. Trim leading/trailing whitespace; require 1-80 Unicode code points after trimming, on the server as well as in the UI. Persist only the signed-in caller's name and show the updated name in the same session and after reload. Treat supplied names as text. Reject invalid/anonymous writes and ignore attempts to change another user's identity, role, email, verification or orders. Preserve sign-in and existing protected pages. No dependency or global auth-cache changes.
A04:
# Task A04: change password creation policy
Require password lengths of 12-128 UTF-16 code units (the existing auth/native-input length convention) for passwords in existing registration and password-reset flows, both UI and direct server API. Existing users with 8-11 character passwords must still sign in. Preserve reset-token expiration and single use, email-verification/auto-sign-in semantics, upper limit 128, identity/role and billing state. Invalid short password attempts must not consume a valid reset token or write a credential. Do not add a separate change-password feature or force password migration. Preserve existing public auth endpoints.
B05:
# Task B05: recognize payment codes inside transfer descriptions
In both signed webhook and polling cron flows, recognize exactly one uppercase marker token SK followed by a code token, anywhere in whitespace-separated transfer content. Code tokens use ASCII letters, digits, underscore and hyphen, length 5-50, with case preserved. More than one SK marker, missing/invalid code, or lowercase sk must not complete any order. Example (hypothetical): BANK SK Ab_123-x REF. Preserve existing QR/checkout content SK <code>, including its space and exact case. Keep signature/cron authentication, ownership, amount matching, terminal-state, audit and duplicate-processing behavior. Do not alter code generation or dependencies. Preserve existing webhook/cron endpoints.
B06:
# Task B06: enforce expiry atomically at payment completion
For a valid incoming matching-code payment of the correct amount, pending orders at or beyond expiresAt must become expired rather than completed even if cleanup has not run. Evaluate server time at the serialized decision to update that order (application or database clock is allowed), not the untrusted payload timestamp. Retain the linked payment audit; expired orders grant no entitlement. An ignored/order_not_pending response is correct for expiry, consistent with existing terminal-state responses. Live pending orders complete; mismatch, unknown and existing terminal orders keep their existing behavior. Make competing cleanup and completion safe: once expired/cancelled/completed, a row cannot be flipped back by a competing payment. For two distinct valid simultaneous payments for the same live order, at most one may report completing it; duplicate transaction IDs retain existing already_processed behavior. This atomic response rule is an explicit new requirement, not a claim about baseline correctness. Preserve existing public webhook/cron entry points, audit semantics, identity, access control, dependencies and the entitlement model.
U02:
# Task U02: admin account detail
Add an accessible link/control from each existing admin-directory row to an independently addressable detail page for that account (a path or query URL is allowed). Display name, email, role, verification state, creation time and the count of all stored session records (including expired records, consistent with the directory baseline). No raw session tokens or unrelated account data. Anonymous/ordinary users cannot access detail even by direct URL; missing target returns a clear not-found response. Reads must not change identity, credentials, roles, orders or sessions; preserve the existing directory. Any implementation/URL is allowed; the detail must be discoverable from the selected directory row. Directory/detail reads follow the baseline session-cache semantics; immediate invalidation of already cached admin reads is not a requirement of this task.
U03:
# Task U03: admin role update
On the existing admin directory, add accessible controls for an administrator to set another account to user or admin and observe persistence after reload. This task starts independently; U02 detail is not present. The new write flow must reject anonymous/ordinary users, invalid roles, forged caller identity and self-demotion, on the server. A caller demoted in the database but retaining a cached admin cookie must be denied writing through this new flow. Preserve all non-role identity/credential/order data and other accounts' roles. Promotion/demotion must affect target permissions on fresh sign-in. Old read-session cache behavior may remain as baseline; do not globally disable caching or promise immediate invalidation. Self-demotion rejection applies to this new feature, not every existing auth API. Native forms or server actions and any correct endpoints are allowed.
common:
## Shared environment and limits
Preserve the supplied layout; no fixed file list is required. Dependencies are preinstalled; do not change dependencies/auth-library internals or globally disable cookie cache. A fresh synthetic PostgreSQL database and Next.js server run at http://localhost:3107. Basic checks: pnpm check-types; pnpm test:run; pnpm build; TEST_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3107 pnpm test:billing; SEPAY_BANK_ACCOUNT=0010000000000 SEPAY_BANK_NAME=Vietcombank pnpm test:sepay-qr-url. Playwright/Chromium are available via require('/opt/behavior/node_modules/playwright'), launch with args ['--no-sandbox']. You may write your own checks.
SePay's external transaction-list service is simulated equally in every condition. /tmp/study-sepay-fixture.json contains the synthetic transaction array; cron uses its usual HTTP endpoint and synthetic credentials from .env. No real email/bank services are configured. Public fixture /tmp/study-clock.json may hold {"now": <milliseconds>} for the application's clock, or null for real time; database time remains real. Do not change these common runtime adapters. Hidden evaluation also tests normal time.
Each task starts from a fresh unsolved snapshot, without any other task's solution. Wall time is 900 seconds from model CLI invocation, including checks. Keep work in /workspace; do not commit. Finish with a concise account of changes/checks. No replacement model attempts are permitted.
